info.text:
A few lines added to the tax code in 1978 now hold about $10.8 trillion in 401(k) plans (ICI, June 2026). This video explains how it happened: Ted Benna's 1980 idea, the IRS's 1981 green light, and how 401(k)-style plans overtook company pensions, from about 19 million active workers in 1980 to about 85 million in 2020 while pensions fell from 30.1 million to 12 million. We break down the risk shift with real math (a $27,000-a-year pension versus the $675,000 a 401(k) would need), how the tax break and match work with the 2026 limits, auto-enrollment from the 2006 law to SECURE 2.0 and the Saver's Match starting with 2027 contributions, and a scorecard on balances and access.

Sources: Investment Company Institute, quarterly retirement market data (Q2 2026) and Fact Book (2025); US Department of Labor, EBSA, Private Pension Plan Bulletin Historical Tables (Sept 2025) and bulletin abstracts (2000, 2011, 2020), via EPI and EBRI; IRS IR-2025-111 / Notice 2025-67 (Nov 13, 2025); IRS vesting rules; Pension Protection Act of 2006 (Aug 17, 2006); SECURE 2.0 Act (Dec 29, 2022) and proposed regulations (Jan 10, 2025); Treasury/IRS Notice 2026-48 on the Saver's Match (Aug 2026); Vanguard, How America Saves 2026 (June 2026); BLS, Employee Benefits in the United States, March 2026 (Sept 25, 2026); CNBC (Jan 4, 2017) and ASPPA (2018) on the 401(k)'s history; Bengen, Journal of Financial Planning (Oct 1994).

News and education, not financial advice.
